Subject: Draft MSA + Order Form — IP and training carveouts

Ben —

Thanks for the draft MSA and the Order Form. Our legal team has reviewed and returned a marked-up copy (attached) with a few priority items we'd like to resolve before procurement can sign:

- Output ownership: we want explicit language that Acme retains exclusive ownership of customer-generated outputs and any derivative products.
- Training / model use: the redlines require a firm "no retraining" commitment unless Acme provides written opt-in.
- Feedback license: we have concerns about a broad feedback license that might let Redwood use identifiable customer outputs for model improvement. We'd prefer a telemetry-only, aggregated, non-identifiable clause.

Can your team propose concrete language for those three buckets? If you prefer a short legal-to-legal call, we can book time this week. Attached: Acme_MSARedlines_20270315.docx (track changes).

Best,
Elena Moreno
Senior Contracts Manager
Acme Health, Inc.

Elena —

Thanks for the marked-up MSA and the clear note. I pulled together a short summary of Redwood's position and a few suggested compromise points (attached). High-level:

- Output ownership: Redwood is happy to confirm customers retain ownership of outputs they submit and the immediate generated outputs. We need narrow rights to operate the service (rendering, caching, telemetry) but are open to carving out downstream productization if Acme requires it for sensitive outputs.
- Training use: Redwood's default is not to retrain on customer content. We only retrain on customer data if a customer explicitly opts in via an order form amendment. We can add explicit opt-in language and a minimum-notice process.
- Feedback/license: we're prepared to limit the feedback license to non-identifiable telemetry, model improvement, and safety work. We can include strong anonymization language and a prohibition on using raw customer outputs for training without opt-in.

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal-to-legal redline exchange: Redwood legal will return a tracked draft with proposed language for the three clauses above.
2) 30-minute sync this Thursday to walk through any sticking points.
3) Narrow the Order Form so any training opt-in is explicit and separately initialed by Acme.

I've attached a short one-page response that I hope covers the position and can be used by your team offline: Redwood_response_summary.pdf (attached).

If that works, I'll escalate to our legal and loop Marissa and Rishi to coordinate timing.

Best,

Ben —

Appreciate the quick reply and the summary. A couple of specific asks from legal after reviewing your note:

- "No retraining unless opt-in": Acme needs a one-sentence warranty in the MSA stating Redwood will not use Acme's Customer Data to train models or improve parameters unless Acme signs an explicit training addendum.
- Downstream productization: Acme is pushing for an express restriction preventing Redwood from selling or licensing products that incorporate Acme-owned outputs. Internal use for improving service is different from commercializing derivative products.
- Feedback license: we need narrower language — telemetry only, aggregated, and no ability to reverse engineer outputs into training datasets.

Legal prefers you propose tracked language they can accept/decline. Can we get a redline by end of day Wednesday? If not, please propose an earliest slot for legal-to-legal tomorrow/Thursday.

Thanks,
Elena

Ben / Rishi —

Looping in a suggested set of short MSA clauses that have worked for other enterprise accounts. Feel free to copy/paste into the redline and then hand to legal. My suggested language (draft):

"Section X.X - Use of Customer Data. Redwood shall not use, disclose, or incorporate Customer Data into any training, model improvement, or parameter updates for any proprietary model or dataset used in Redwood's commercial systems without the Customer's prior written consent, executed as a separate training addendum to this Agreement. For clarity, 'Customer Data' includes all inputs, outputs, logs, and metadata provided by or generated for the Customer.

Section X.Y - Feedback and Telemetry. Redwood may collect operational telemetry (latency, error rates, anonymized usage patterns) for the purposes of monitoring, improving service reliability, and debugging. Such telemetry shall be processed in aggregate form and shall not include raw customer outputs, personal data, or any data that would allow re-identification of Customer Data.

Section X.Z - Output Ownership. Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data and any outputs generated through the Service. Redwood's rights are limited to those necessary to provide the Service and to fulfill obligations under this Agreement.

"

These are intentionally short, and we can iterate. Once Ben has the redline from Elena's team, Rishi and I will prioritize a legal-to-legal exchange.

Marissa Cole
VP, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
